outcome: The general case (extending Kronecker-Weber to an arbitrary base number field) remains open; the only substantial resolution in the area, Dasgupta-Kakde's construction of the maximal abelian extension of totally real fields via Brumer-Stark units, predates the frozen revision (arXiv preprints 2020-2021, Annals of Mathematics 2023).
summary: Hilbert's twelfth problem, in the general form stated in the bullet (extend Kronecker-Weber to an arbitrary base number field), remains open, and I found no result since 26 January 2024 that changes what this bullet's entry should say. The one major resolution in this area — Dasgupta and Kakde's construction of the maximal abelian extension of totally real number fields from Brumer-Stark units, via a proof of the p-part of the integral Gross-Stark conjecture — predates the window: their preprint 'Brumer-Stark Units and Hilbert's 12th Problem' is arXiv:2103.02516 (submitted March 2021, an earlier related preprint from 2020), and it was published in Annals of Mathematics in 2023. The current live Wikipedia article and a June 2026 Simons Foundation retrospective on the status of all 23 Hilbert problems ('Solved, Unsolved and Unsolvable') both confirm the general case is still labeled unresolved, with only special cases (imaginary quadratic/CM fields via classical complex multiplication, and totally real fields via Dasgupta-Kakde) settled. Post-window activity I found is limited to: (1) an ICMS workshop 'Recent Progress on Hilbert's 12th Problem' held 24-28 June 2024 in Edinburgh, built around a lecture series by Dasgupta and Kakde presenting their (already-published/preprinted) totally-real-field result to a wider audience — this is dissemination of pre-2024 work, not a new result; (2) arXiv:2505.22272, a 4-page addendum (May 2025) to a much older paper ('Measured foliations and Hilbert 12th problem,' arXiv:0804.0057, published in Acta Mathematica Vietnamica 2023) giving numerical/computational examples of abelian extensions of real quadratic fields under Darmon-Vonk-style conjectural constructions — a small computational illustration of an existing conjectural framework, not a settled case and not clearly in scope of the stated bullet even if it were new; (3) arXiv:2408.02158 (August 2024), 'Ultra-Galois theory and an analogue of the Kronecker-Weber theorem for rational function fields over ultra-finite fields' — this proves a Kronecker-Weber analogue for a different object entirely (rational function fields over ultraproducts of finite fields, not number fields), so under §3.1 it is a related/variant problem sharing a namesake theorem, not a case of the number-field problem stated in this bullet, and does not count as scope. No source anywhere associates any AI system with this problem; a search for a possible AI connection surfaced only an unrelated Apple ML Research project literally named 'Hilbert' (an agentic LLM+Lean theorem-proving framework), which has no connection to Hilbert's twelfth problem and is a pure name coincidence. I agree with the triage's verdict and its underlying reasoning.
competing_reading: One could argue the Darmon-Pozzi-Vonk program for real quadratic fields (referenced in older seminar descriptions and now illustrated numerically in arXiv:2505.22272) constitutes 'partial' progress if the addendum's computations were novel confirmations extending the conjectural framework. But the addendum itself dates its core theoretical content to a 2023 journal publication of a 2008 preprint, and its 2025 content is purely numerical verification of examples rather than a new theorem, so it does not rise to a case being settled.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or announcement, dated after 26 January 2024, either (a) proving unconditionally that a specific analytic construction generates the maximal abelian extension for some broad new class of number fields beyond totally real/CM fields (e.g., a real quadratic field result upgraded from conjectural to proven), or (b) a full proof for the fully general case. Also useful: any statement from an AI lab or paper's authors crediting an AI system with producing part of such a proof.
